candidate.name: Ardent
candidate.one_liner: Postgres sandboxes in seconds with zero migration

provenance.title: Launch HN: Ardent (YC P26) – Postgres sandboxes in seconds with zero migration

facts.statement: Ardent describes its product as enabling creation of copies of any Postgres database in under 6 seconds, letting coding agents test, clean, and migrate data on isolated branches with zero risk to production.
facts.value: Postgres sandboxes in seconds with zero migration

facts.statement: Ardent's product is designed to let coding agents test their database code on isolated, near-production-like sandboxes to prevent errors that could impact production databases.
facts.value: Let coding agents test database code safely

facts.statement: Ardent's product depends on recent developments in logical replication and copy-on-write branching technology implemented by providers like neon, allowing near-instant clones of Postgres databases even at terabyte scale.
facts.value: logical replication + copy-on-write scaling technologies circa early 2020s

facts.statement: Ardent sits as a hosted service that replicates production Postgres databases into read replicas, then creates isolated branches from those replicas, presenting them as full Postgres databases accessible with standard connection URLs.
facts.value: hosted read replica and branching service

facts.statement: Users can start using Ardent's product for free, including signing up and getting started with isolated Postgres branches without mandatory sales contact.
Ardent publishes pricing information with a free Starter tier, a Scale tier at $250 per month plus usage, and Enterprise pricing available with custom plans.
facts.value: public pricing with free, scale, and enterprise tiers

facts.statement: Ardent's Hacker News launch post received 99 points and 52 comments three months prior to August 23, 2026.
Zennagents CTO Akshendra Garg publicly stated that Ardent allows their agents to test in seconds with zero drift from production data.
Chevron's Head of Data, Abhay Singh, described Ardent as a fundamental shift in how agents and developers work with databases, comparing its importance to Git for code.
facts.value: Chevron Head of Data Abhay Singh

facts.statement: Openledger CEO Pryce Yebesi said Ardent lets them move as fast as agents write code without worrying about agents working on the database layer.
Vikram is a named founder of Ardent.
Evan is a named founder of Ardent with 12 years prior experience in data engineering.
facts.value: Evan, founder with 12 years data engineering experience

disqualifiers.statement: The team is named and nothing any of them is stated to have built appears in the evidence, and the company has no public repository.

why_this_call.text: Pass — disqualifier D-1 fired, and a cited disqualifier forces a pass whatever the score (71/100, 100% coverage).
The largest shortfall is D1 Founder–market fit & technical depth at 12/25 (band 6–12).

bullets.text: Vikram is a named founder of Ardent.
Evan is a named founder of Ardent with 12 years prior experience in data engineering.

Ardent describes its product as enabling creation of copies of any Postgres database in under 6 seconds, letting coding agents test, clean, and migrate data on isolated branches with zero risk to production.
Ardent's product is designed to let coding agents test their database code on isolated, near-production-like sandboxes to prevent errors that could impact production databases.

Ardent sits as a hosted service that replicates production Postgres databases into read replicas, then creates isolated branches from those replicas, presenting them as full Postgres databases accessible with standard connection URLs.
Users can start using Ardent's product for free, including signing up and getting started with isolated Postgres branches without mandatory sales contact.
Ardent publishes pricing information with a free Starter tier, a Scale tier at $250 per month plus usage, and Enterprise pricing available with custom plans.

Ardent's product depends on recent developments in logical replication and copy-on-write branching technology implemented by providers like neon, allowing near-instant clones of Postgres databases even at terabyte scale.
Zennagents CTO Akshendra Garg publicly stated that Ardent allows their agents to test in seconds with zero drift from production data.
Chevron's Head of Data, Abhay Singh, described Ardent as a fundamental shift in how agents and developers work with databases, comparing its importance to Git for code.
Openledger CEO Pryce Yebesi said Ardent lets them move as fast as agents write code without worrying about agents working on the database layer.
Ardent's Hacker News launch post received 99 points and 52 comments three months prior to August 23, 2026.
Disqualifier D-1 — The team is named and nothing any of them is stated to have built appears in the evidence, and the company has no public repository.

what_would_change_my_mind.text: Disqualifier D-1: find a stated prior role for somebody they name, something one of them is stated to have built, or a public repository. It would then no longer hold, and the call would no longer be forced to Pass.
D1 Founder–market fit & technical depth: find a prior employer, role or period stated for somebody the company names. That moves it from 6–12 to 13–19 (+7).
D3 Evidence of pull: find a second credible signal — over 200 stars, a named user, a named integration — with the repository pushed inside 90 days. That moves it from 6–12 to 13–19 (+7).
